Abstract.AbstractText: A cercomonad, tentatively named Phytocercomonas venanatans Ngo, Braithwaite and Bass, is confirmed as the cause of the sugarcane disease chlorotic streak. This was achieved by establishing aseptic liquid cultures of the pathogen isolated from internal pieces of sugarcane stalk tissue. Actively motile cultures of the pathogen were inoculated into sugarcane roots, stalks and leaf whorls. Infected plants subsequently developed the characteristic symptoms of chlorotic streak. Infection was confirmed by PCR screening of plant tissues and by reisolation of the pathogen into aseptic culture followed by PCR and microscopic confirmation. P. venanatans is the first reported pathogenic cercomonad able to systemically infect higher plants and the first plant pathogenic cercozoan able to be successfully grown in axenic culture on common microbiological media.
